questions.stem: How is Big Data best characterised in relation to a data lake?
options: Big Data is a single storage system; the data lake is its query engine
Big Data is the broader ecosystem and paradigm; the data lake is a specific repository within it
Big Data is a subset of the data lake
They are two names for the same thing
Big Data is a vendor product; the data lake is open source
questions.explanation: Big Data is the movement and ecosystem of technologies and practices, whereas a data lake is a specific architectural component that grew out of that movement.

questions.stem: Which challenges did the Big Data ecosystem arise to address?
options: The three Vs: volume, velocity and variety
Table locking in OLTP
Cross-border data storage
Slow tape archives
Encryption key management
questions.explanation: Big Data arose to address the challenges posed by the three Vs, volume, velocity and variety, of modern data.

questions.stem: Which of the following belongs to the Big Data toolbox rather than being the data lake itself?
options: A raw transaction log archive
Cloud object storage
Spark, Kafka and NoSQL databases
A schema-on-read repository
Historical feature data sets
questions.explanation: Big Data includes distributed storage and processing technologies such as HDFS, MapReduce, Spark and Kafka, plus new database types; the lake is the storage repository.

questions.stem: What does the data lake embody as one of Big Data's core principles?
options: The ability to enforce a predefined model before loading
The ability to capture everything without forcing predefined models
The ability to run ACID transactions
The ability to encrypt everything at rest
The ability to process only structured data
questions.explanation: The data lake is the storage paradigm that embodies Big Data's principle of capturing everything, without forcing predefined models, using schema-on-read.

questions.stem: In terms of purpose, how do Big Data and a data lake differ?
options: Big Data provides cheap storage; the data lake solves scale and speed
Big Data focuses on solving the challenges of scale, speed and diversity; the data lake provides a place to store all forms of data cheaply and flexibly
Both focus only on real-time streaming
Big Data is for governance; the data lake is for analytics
Big Data is for structured data; the data lake is for unstructured data only
questions.explanation: Big Data focuses on solving scale, speed and diversity challenges, while the data lake provides a cheap, flexible place to store all forms of data.

questions.stem: On what is a data lake usually built?
options: A relational database with star schemas
HDFS or cloud object storage with query engines layered on top
An in-memory cache
A message queue
A tape library
questions.explanation: A data lake is usually built on HDFS or cloud object storage, with query engines layered on top.

questions.stem: In the streaming fraud detection example, which component belongs to the data lake rather than the Big Data ecosystem?
options: Kafka for real-time ingestion
Spark for processing
NoSQL databases for rapid lookups
Raw transaction logs, enriched data sets and historical features used to train models
The banking application itself
questions.explanation: The Big Data ecosystem supplies Kafka, Spark and NoSQL; the data lake stores the raw transaction logs, enriched data sets and historical features data scientists use to build and retrain models.

questions.stem: Which misconception does understanding the Big Data versus data lake distinction help avoid?
options: That data lakes require 3NF
That simply building a data lake equals doing Big Data
That Big Data cannot use SQL
That Kafka is a storage system
That warehouses are obsolete
questions.explanation: The lake is one piece of a larger landscape that includes ingestion, processing, governance and analytics, so building a lake alone is not the same as doing Big Data.

questions.stem: How does the evolution of Big Data relate to data lakes?
options: Data lakes were invented first and led to Big Data
Big Data drove the innovation that made data lakes possible, and lakes became the storage foundation for modern analytics, machine learning and AI
They evolved independently and only later converged
Data lakes replaced Big Data once Hadoop declined
Neither influenced the other
questions.explanation: Big Data drove the innovation that made data lakes possible; data lakes then became the practical storage foundation for modern analytics, machine learning and AI.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a type of new database introduced by the Big Data movement?
options: NoSQL
Graph
Document
Columnar
Hierarchical
questions.explanation: The new database types named are NoSQL, graph, document and columnar; hierarchical databases are not among them.
